title: The Brunei Half Marathon 2026: Racing Across the Iconic SHOAS Bridge
seo_title: Brunei Half Marathon 2026 Review: SHOAS Bridge Run
meta_description: An honest look at the 2026 Brunei Half Marathon on the SHOAS Bridge — course, dates, entry fees, kit and whether it's worth the trip to Bandar Seri Begawan.
dek: A race staged entirely on one of Southeast Asia's most photogenic bridges, backed by an airline and a three-year plan — but still a young event finding its organisational footing.
verdict: The Brunei Half Marathon's whole appeal is structural: you don't run past a landmark, you run across one, crossing the full span of the SHOAS Bridge between Brunei-Muara and Temburong districts. Backed by Royal Brunei Airlines and Arrowtech Sports as the opening act of a three-year build toward a 2027 marathon, it drew a respectable debut crowd and ministerial fanfare in 2025, even if turnout fell short of the organisers' original target. It suits travellers chasing a genuinely novel bridge-run bragging right more than runners hunting a fast, seasoned, big-field production.

sections.heading: One Bridge, One Unforgettable Route
paragraphs: The whole draw of this race is that it doesn't tour a city's landmarks — it runs on top of one. Every distance is staged on the Sultan Haji Omar 'Ali Saifuddien Bridge, and finishers get <cite index="42-3">the opportunity to cross the entire structure of the Sultan Haji Omar Ali Saifuddien Bridge connecting the Brunei Muara District and the Temburong District, which has become an icon of the country's infrastructure</cite> [5]. Organisers were explicit from the launch that this was <cite index="11-1">the first time the nation's most iconic landmark will host a major sporting event</cite> [3].

That point-to-point structure shows up in the small logistical details too — the half marathon's entitlements list includes a <cite index="25-2">Free Return Shuttle Service from Event Village to SHOAS Bridge</cite> [1], a reminder that you're racing across a crossing rather than looping through downtown streets.

sections.heading: Format, Distances and Start Times
paragraphs: The event launched in 2025 with three options — a half marathon plus <cite index="16-4">a 10km, and 3km Fun Run, making it an event for everyone in the community</cite> [1] — and for 2026 the organisers have confirmed the race returns across the weekend of 21 and 22 November, with the shortest leg swapped up to a 5km alongside the 21.1km half and 10km <cite index="1-1">Run on the iconic SHOAS Bridge 21 & 22 November 2026 21.1 KM | 10 KM | 5KM</cite> [2].

Race-morning specifics from the debut edition give a sense of what to expect: the 10km started at <cite index="26-5">Start Time 7:00AM Cut Off Time 2 hrs 30min</cite> [1], while the half marathon's own start time was left <cite index="25-2">To be confirmed (subject to authorities' approval)</cite> [1] until closer to race day — worth factoring in if you're booking flights early.

sections.heading: Entry Fees and What's Included
paragraphs: Half marathon entry for the debut year ran at <cite index="25-3">Early Bird BND 95 Standard BND 100</cite> [1], with the shorter 10km listed separately at <cite index="49-4">10KM Registration Fee BND 85</cite> [1] — reasonable pricing for a race with international ambitions.

The kit list is generous for the entry price: half marathon finishers within the cut-off are promised a race shirt, a separate finisher's shirt, a drawstring bag, microfibre towel, energy gel, finisher's medal, a mileage credit toward Royal Brunei Airlines' loyalty programme, an e-certificate, event photography and a BND10 voucher on top of the shuttle service <cite index="25-2">2XU Race Shirt 2XU Finisher's Shirt* Drawstring Bag Microfiber Towel Energy Gel Finisher's Medal* Royal Skies Miles E-Certificate Photography Free Return Shuttle Service from Event Village to SHOAS Bridge BND10 Voucher</cite> [1].

sections.heading: An Airline-Backed, Three-Year Build
paragraphs: This isn't a one-off; it's phase one of a longer plan. The organisers describe <cite index="14-4">the start of a three-year strategic partnership, the collaboration will feature Half-Marathon events in 2025 and 2026, culminating in a Full Marathon in 2027</cite> [4], with Royal Brunei Airlines and Arrowtech Sports signed on as the headline partners.

The framing from both partners leans heavily on national pride and tourism rather than pure competition: Royal Brunei Airlines said the tie-up <cite index="11-5">places Brunei's most recognisable bridge on the global stage as the backdrop for a world-class half-marathon</cite> [3], while Arrowtech Sports' general manager added that the event represents <cite index="11-6">not just sport, but also wellness, tourism and national pride</cite> [3].

sections.heading: Debut Turnout and National-Event Energy
paragraphs: Ahead of the launch, organisers said they were <cite index="11-2">targeting around 5,000 participants from Brunei and abroad</cite> [3]. The actual debut fell a bit short of that but was still substantial for a first-year event, with reports noting it <cite index="42-1">successfully organised the world's most prestigious event, attracting more than three thousand participants locally and abroad</cite> [5].

It carries genuine government-level weight for a young race: the half marathon's flag-off <cite index="42-5">was held by Yang Berhormat Pehin Datu Lailaraja Retired Major General Dato Paduka Seri Awang Haji Halbi bin Haji Mohammad Yussof, Minister at the Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister of Defence</cite> [5], and awards were presented by ministers rather than event staff — the kind of ceremony that gives a debut race an outsized sense of occasion.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: Eligibility is straightforward but worth checking before you enter: the half marathon requires runners to be <cite index="25-2">18 years old or older on race day</cite> [1], while the 10km category is open to anyone <cite index="26-5">15 years old or older on race day</cite> [1].

If you want a bucket-list photo mid-span over open water and you're comfortable with a race that's still only in its second year — meaning start times and finer logistics may shift closer to the date — this is a strong pick, especially framed against the longer-term promise of a 2027 marathon on the same bridge <cite index="14-4">culminating in a Full Marathon in 2027</cite> [4]. Runners chasing a big, seasoned international field or guaranteed early-locked schedules may want to wait a couple more editions before committing.

faqs.question: When is the Brunei Half Marathon 2026?
faqs.answer: The event is scheduled across the weekend of 21 and 22 November 2026 in Bandar Seri Begawan, continuing the two-day structure organisers used for the 2025 debut on the SHOAS Bridge, with the half marathon as the headline distance.

faqs.question: What distances can I run at the Brunei Half Marathon?
faqs.answer: The 2026 edition offers a 21.1km half marathon, a 10km, and a 5km, all staged on the Sultan Haji Omar 'Ali Saifuddien Bridge. This replaces the shortest 3km fun run offered when the event launched in 2025.

faqs.question: Where does the Brunei Half Marathon course run?
faqs.answer: The entire race takes place on the SHOAS Bridge, which connects Brunei-Muara District to Temburong District. It's the country's most recognisable piece of infrastructure and, per organisers, the first time it has hosted a major sporting event.

faqs.question: Is the Brunei Half Marathon a big race?
faqs.answer: It's a growing national event rather than an established mega-race: organisers targeted around 5,000 entrants for the 2025 debut and drew more than 3,000 runners, with a ministerial flag-off and prize presentation underscoring its national profile.
